features.name: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Does the OP's argument include a direct personal anecdote, meaning the OP recounts their own specific experience or event?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's body; not the title). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, recounts at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific experience, event or episode that happened to the OP personally (e.g., 'when I worked at...', 'my friend and I once...' where OP was involved). Return 0 if the argument has only general claims, hypotheticals, opinions, or others' experiences/quotations not adopted as OP's own experience. Quotation marks alone do not indicate another speaker. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits, resolution updates or reports of the outcome as anecdotes. Empty argument gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

h0: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Posts with op_argument_has_personal_anecdote = 1 have a lower probability of OP view change than those with 0.
note: Presence is binary (unspecified quantity). Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements; the prompt excludes those as anecdote evidence, but timing relative to outcome is unknown. OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model; association only, not causal.
